seo.title: 30 Common Mistakes NFT Developers Make (And How to Avoid Them)
seo.description: Learn from the mistakes of others. A comprehensive guide to the most common errors NFT developers make in smart contracts, metadata, and launch strategy.

content.intro: NFT development combines smart contract security with art, metadata, and launch logistics. Here are the most common mistakes that cost NFT developers money, reputation, or both.

mistakes.title: Using sequential token IDs for reveal
mistakes.description: Predictable token IDs let snipers identify rare NFTs before reveal by watching metadata.
mistakes.solution: Use randomized assignment with Chainlink VRF or commit-reveal schemes.

mistakes.title: No reentrancy protection on mint
mistakes.description: Mint functions with callbacks (like safe transfers) can be exploited for extra mints.
mistakes.solution: Use ReentrancyGuard and checks-effects-interactions pattern.

mistakes.title: Integer overflow in batch minting
mistakes.description: Pre-0.8.0 contracts without SafeMath could overflow mint counters.
mistakes.solution: Use Solidity 0.8+ or implement proper overflow checks.

mistakes.title: Unchecked array lengths in airdrops
mistakes.description: Airdrop functions without length limits can exceed block gas limit.
mistakes.solution: Batch airdrops with reasonable limits per transaction.

mistakes.title: Allowing mints to contracts without callback check
mistakes.description: Minting to non-ERC721Receiver contracts locks tokens permanently.
mistakes.solution: Use safeMint or implement receiver checks.

mistakes.title: Storing allowlist on-chain
mistakes.description: On-chain arrays are expensive and can be manipulated by watching transactions.
mistakes.solution: Use Merkle trees for gas-efficient, tamper-proof allowlists.

mistakes.title: No per-wallet mint limits on allowlist
mistakes.description: Allowlisted addresses can transfer their spot to others or mint multiple times.
mistakes.solution: Track mints per address and enforce limits.

mistakes.title: Merkle proof replay attacks
mistakes.description: Valid proofs can be reused if contract doesn't track used proofs.
mistakes.solution: Mark addresses as claimed after successful mint.

mistakes.title: Allowlist signature without expiry
mistakes.description: Signed allowlist entries without expiry can be used indefinitely.
mistakes.solution: Include expiry timestamp in signed messages.

mistakes.title: Front-runnable signature reveals
mistakes.description: Signatures revealed in pending transactions can be stolen.
mistakes.solution: Tie signatures to specific msg.sender addresses.

mistakes.title: Centralized metadata hosting
mistakes.description: Traditional hosting means metadata disappears if server goes down.
mistakes.solution: Use IPFS, Arweave, or on-chain storage for permanence.

mistakes.title: Mutable metadata without transparency
mistakes.description: Ability to change metadata after mint destroys trust.
mistakes.solution: Use provenance hash and freeze metadata after reveal.

mistakes.title: No provenance hash
mistakes.description: Without provenance, you cannot prove art was finalized before minting.
mistakes.solution: Hash all metadata/images and publish before mint starts.

mistakes.title: Incorrect token URI implementation
mistakes.description: Returning wrong URI format breaks marketplace display.
mistakes.solution: Test on OpenSea testnet before mainnet. Follow metadata standards.

mistakes.title: Large image files
mistakes.description: Large files slow loading and increase IPFS pinning costs.
mistakes.solution: Optimize images. Use proper compression. Consider thumbnails.

mistakes.title: Using block.timestamp for randomness
mistakes.description: Miners can manipulate timestamps within bounds. Not truly random.
mistakes.solution: Use Chainlink VRF for verifiable randomness.

mistakes.title: Predictable blockhash randomness
mistakes.description: blockhash(block.number) is always 0. blockhash of past blocks can be known.
mistakes.solution: Use commit-reveal or Chainlink VRF.

mistakes.title: Single-transaction reveal
mistakes.description: Reveals in same transaction as mint let attackers simulate and cherry-pick.
mistakes.solution: Separate mint and reveal into different transactions/blocks.

mistakes.title: Insufficient randomness entropy
mistakes.description: Combining weak entropy sources doesn't make strong randomness.
mistakes.solution: Use cryptographically secure randomness from oracles.

mistakes.title: Owner can rug-pull funds
mistakes.description: Arbitrary withdrawal functions let owners steal mint proceeds.
mistakes.solution: Use transparent withdrawal to known addresses or multi-sig.

mistakes.title: No withdrawal function
mistakes.description: Forgetting to include a withdrawal function locks ETH in contract forever.
mistakes.solution: Always test withdrawal on testnet before mainnet deploy.

mistakes.title: Single owner key
mistakes.description: One compromised key loses entire collection control.
mistakes.solution: Use multi-sig for owner functions.

mistakes.title: Pausable without unpause
mistakes.description: Some contracts can be paused but have no unpause function.
mistakes.solution: Ensure all pausable functionality can be reversed.

mistakes.title: No on-chain royalty support
mistakes.description: Without EIP-2981, royalties depend on marketplace voluntary enforcement.
mistakes.solution: Implement EIP-2981 royaltyInfo function.

mistakes.title: Immutable royalty recipient
mistakes.description: Cannot update royalty address if wallet is compromised.
mistakes.solution: Make royalty recipient updateable by owner/multi-sig.

mistakes.title: Excessive royalty percentages
mistakes.description: Very high royalties encourage marketplace bypass.
mistakes.solution: Keep royalties reasonable. 5-10% is standard.

mistakes.title: No gas optimization
mistakes.description: High gas costs during popular mints price out regular users.
mistakes.solution: Use ERC721A for batch minting. Optimize storage operations.

mistakes.title: Unverified contract on Etherscan
mistakes.description: Unverified contracts look suspicious and reduce trust.
mistakes.solution: Verify source code immediately after deployment.

mistakes.title: No testnet testing
mistakes.description: Deploying directly to mainnet without thorough testing.
mistakes.solution: Test extensively on Goerli/Sepolia. Test OpenSea display.

mistakes.title: Wrong network deployment
mistakes.description: Accidentally deploying to wrong network or testnet with real funds.
mistakes.solution: Double-check network ID in deployment scripts.
